notice: RN bank batch 150: Pediatric case studies: catch-up vaccines, infant meningitis, foreign body aspiration and lead poisoning, with four standalone items. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md.

questions.stem: A child arrives at the emergency department with sudden breathing trouble. Using the note, fill in the bowtie: the most likely problem in the middle, two actions to take now on the left and two parameters to monitor on the right.

actions.text: Look in the throat with a tongue blade to see the epiglottis
Lay the child flat on the stretcher for a neck x-ray
Take a throat culture now before antibiotics start

rationale.correct: Drooling, tripod position and high fever in an unvaccinated child is epiglottitis; protect the airway.

perOption.c1: Sudden high fever, drooling, tripod position, muffled voice, unvaccinated.
perOption.c4: No choking episode and high fever.
perOption.a5: Wait until the airway is secure.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: In a pediatric emergency department, four children arrive at the same time. Which child should the nurse see first?

options.text: A 3-year-old who choked on a grape and now cannot speak or cry
A 7-year-old with an obvious forearm deformity after falling off a swing at school
A 10-month-old with fever of 39 C who is feeding and smiling
A 5-year-old with a 2 cm scalp cut that is still oozing blood

rationale.correct: A child who cannot speak or cry after choking has complete obstruction.

perOption.a: Complete airway obstruction needs immediate action.

caseStudies.title: Catch-up vaccination for a newly arrived child

exhibits.title: Pediatric clinic
exhibits.body: A 4-year-old child arrived from another country a month ago with no vaccine records. The child has a mild cold with a temperature of 37.6 C. The parent says the child had a rash after eating eggs once. A younger sibling is getting chemotherapy for leukemia.

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 6-month-old infant has had a fever of 39.6 C for a day, poor feeding and vomiting. The infant is irritable and cries more when picked up. The infant attends daycare.

cells: Cloudy, high WBC, low glucose, high protein
